name: Product Identity
tagline: Issuer-backed records for individual product units across physical and commercial journeys.
problem: A SKU identifies a product model rather than an individual item, leaving brands without a reliable record of unit registration, sale and warranty events across sales channels.
scenario: A brand assigns a unique product-unit record and verification credential, then a customer can query issuer-supplied records without receiving sensitive purchaser information.
differentiation: The planned approach keeps issuance, tenant membership, public verification and warranty data as separate boundaries, so a printed QR identifier never substitutes for trusted physical assurance.
architecture: Channel adapter or CSV -> authenticated organization-scoped API -> serial and unit model -> database -> public verification portal with privacy-limited responses.
limitations: This is pre-MVP design and market validation. A copied QR label does not authenticate a physical object, and customer adoption, external integrations and final warranty workflows remain unverified.
